# osx



macOS-only module for host-scoped system settings: applies `defaults write`
settings and reads every write back to verify it landed.

The module is inert on every other platform. `config/main.zsh` selects the
darwin or linux config from `$OSTYPE`, and every setting the module drives
lives in a macOS `defaults` domain.

Package and cask installation is NOT part of this module. It delegates to
`apps::packages::install` from `zsh/modules/apps/`, which already performs
installation correctly through `core::ensure`. The former `osx::packages`
entry point was a dead stub with zero callers in the source, so
reimplementing installation here would violate the Core Reuse rule.

The 130 unique user-domain defaults (164 non-privileged write calls) this
module does not configure belong to `darwin-system-config` via nix-darwin.
This module's scope is the residual nix-darwin cannot express. 



## Features

- Applies host-scoped `defaults` writes and reads each one back, reporting `written` and `verified` as separate counts
- Delegates package and cask installation to `apps::packages::install` in `zsh/modules/apps/` instead of reimplementing it
- Reports a denied write rather than assuming it applied, so a silent TCC refusal cannot pass unnoticed
- Gates the destructive Dock wipe behind `ZSH_OSX_DESTRUCTIVE` and takes no automatic backup
- Reports the 12 privileged operations as manual procedures instead of running `sudo`
- Manual-only rollback: `defaults write` persists in the user plist, so disabling the module does not revert applied settings






## Requirements

- macOS: the module is inert on other platforms, and a Linux host loads it with no effect
- zsh (loaded as part of dotfiles zsh modules)
- Full Disk Access for the terminal, where a CLI process needs it to write certain preference
  domains. A denied write can fail silently, which is why every write is read back and verified
  rather than trusted
- `defaults export com.apple.dock -` run BEFORE enabling the Dock wipe. The wipe is destructive and
  the module takes no automatic backup; recovery afterwards is manual, by re-dragging the icons
- A prior `defaults export -` of any domain the module is allowed to modify, because restoration
  cannot be scripted from the module itself
- Knowledge that rollback is manual: `defaults write` persists in the user plist, so setting
  `ZSH_OSX_ENABLED=false`, adding `osx` to `ZSH_DISABLED_MODULES`, or deleting the module directory
  does NOT revert any setting already applied. There is no `defaults undo` and the module does not
  build one; restoring a value means reading it with `defaults read` and setting it back by hand
